tests.description: Menus nest. A Contact page filed under an "About" dropdown is an ordinary shape, and a resolver that only walked the top level would silently fall back and point the footer somewhere the editor did not choose.
tests.key: resolveContactUrl › finds a Contact item nested under a dropdown parent

tests.description: The whole reason this reads the nav instead of hardcoding a path: an editor who moves the page in the CMS must move the footer link with it. Hardcoding '/contact' passes every other test here and fails this one.
tests.key: resolveContactUrl › follows a Contact item that has been moved to a different url

tests.description: Case is the editor's business, not ours: "CONTACT" in a shouty menu and "contact" in a lowercase one both mean the same page.
tests.key: resolveContactUrl › matches the label case-insensitively

tests.description: Label beats url, and only a nav containing BOTH kinds of edit can prove it. A single-pass implementation in item order would return '/contact' here, which is the entry the editor renamed AWAY from the contact page.
tests.key: resolveContactUrl › prefers the label match over a url match when the nav contains both

tests.description: The shipped nav. This is the case the footer hits on every page of the real site, so if it ever stops resolving, every footer link breaks at once.
tests.key: resolveContactUrl › resolves the default About + Contact nav to the contact page

tests.description: A dropdown parent has no url, so a naive `find` on the label would return it and put href="undefined" in every footer. The parent is a heading; the answer is the child beneath it.
tests.key: resolveContactUrl › skips a url-less dropdown parent rather than returning undefined

tests.description: With neither override present (a real production build), the site reads its committed `src/content` — so deploys are unaffected.
tests.key: resolveContentRoot › defaults to _projectRoot_/src/content when no override is present

tests.description: With no env var, the sidecar file the editor writes is the load-bearing override for a PTY-launched dev server that didn't inherit the env.
tests.key: resolveContentRoot › falls back to the .codeyam/tmp/content-root sidecar

tests.description: The env override wins outright — this is the programmatic-launch path where the editor injects the absolute sandbox content dir.
tests.key: resolveContentRoot › prefers the CODEYAM_CONTENT_ROOT env override

tests.description: The data root resolves with the same env → sidecar → default precedence as the content root, defaulting to committed `src/data` in production.
tests.key: resolveDataRoot › defaults to _projectRoot_/src/data when no override is present

tests.description: An unseeded component should be stable across builds, not random.
tests.key: resolveTreeSeed › falls back to one shared default tree when given nothing

tests.description: This is the per-page axis: the key decides the tree.
tests.key: resolveTreeSeed › hashes the key when no seed is given

tests.description: An explicit seed is how the variations sheet pins specific trees.
tests.key: resolveTreeSeed › prefers an explicit seed over the key

tests.description: Zero is a legitimate seed and must not be treated as absent.
tests.key: resolveTreeSeed › treats a zero seed as explicit

tests.description: A deeper heading INSIDE a section does not make the page two sections.
tests.key: sectionCount › counts only the section depth in a mixed body

tests.description: `h3` is the section heading in this site's bodies.
tests.key: sectionCount › counts the depth-3 headings

tests.description: The page title is rendered by the header, not the body, so an `h1` in the markdown is not a section.
tests.key: sectionCount › ignores headings at other depths

tests.description: The empty body — a page an editor created but has not written into.
tests.key: sectionCount › reports zero for a body with no headings at all

tests.description: Different seeds diverge, so the seed is a real dial.
tests.key: seededRandom › produces a different sequence for a different seed

tests.description: Same seed, same sequence — this is what keeps the static build reproducible.
tests.key: seededRandom › produces the same sequence for the same seed

tests.description: Values stay in the unit interval, which the jitter maths assumes.
tests.key: seededRandom › stays within zero and one

tests.description: Whatever the step leaves over, the path lands exactly on its endpoint.
tests.key: sinePath › lands exactly on the end even when step does not divide the width

tests.description: A smaller step samples more finely and yields more points.
tests.key: sinePath › samples more densely with a smaller step

tests.description: The wave starts on its baseline: sin(0) is 0, so no vertical offset.
tests.key: sinePath › starts on the baseline

tests.description: fraction is the incompleteness dial — below 1 the wave stops short of the frame.
tests.key: sinePath › stops short of the full width when fraction is below 1

tests.description: Different pages must get different fields, or the per-page axis is a lie.
tests.key: tessellate › gives different seeds different fields

tests.description: Same seed, same scatter — the per-page axis depends on it.
tests.key: tessellate › is reproducible for a seed

tests.description: The unresolved sites are removed BEFORE the partition, not hidden after it. That is the whole effect: the surrounding cells are computed as though those points were never there, so they genuinely overrun where a boundary should be. Excluded afterwards you would have a correct partition with a dot on it.
tests.key: tessellate › leaves the unresolved sites out of the partition entirely

tests.description: A cell around an unresolved point must actually claim that point's ground — this is what makes the omission visible rather than merely true.
tests.key: tessellate › lets a cell overrun the ground an unresolved site would have owned

tests.description: Exactly one cell is opened — the three-sided-square idea at the scale of a territory. Two would read as a pattern; none would read as finished.
tests.key: tessellate › opens exactly one cell

tests.description: A single point is a move with no line — the degenerate but valid case.
tests.key: toPath › emits only a moveto for one point

tests.description: An empty point list has no path to draw, and must not emit a bare "M".
tests.key: toPath › returns an empty string for no points

tests.description: Float noise is rounded so generated paths stay readable in devtools.
tests.key: toPath › rounds coordinates to two decimals

tests.description: The trunk is always walked, so the figure is never empty.
tests.key: treeSegments › always draws the trunk

tests.description: A different seed grows a visibly different tree.
tests.key: treeSegments › grows a different tree for a different seed

tests.description: With no chance of branching, only the trunk exists.
tests.key: treeSegments › grows no side branches when branchChance is zero

tests.description: Same seed, same tree — otherwise every build would redraw the artwork.
tests.key: treeSegments › is deterministic for a given seed

tests.description: The named bare limb carries no children — the deliberate missing piece.
tests.key: treeSegments › leaves the named limb bare

tests.description: Depth bounds the recursion, so a deeper tree is never smaller.
tests.key: treeSegments › never shrinks as depth increases

tests.description: Limbs taper as they divide, so the trunk reads heavier than its branches.
tests.key: treeSegments › tapers stroke width with depth

tests.description: The fixed parameters set the figure's weight and scale, not how it grew.
tests.key: treeVariant › holds the fixed parameters constant across seeds

tests.description: Same seed, same tree — otherwise every build would redraw the artwork.
tests.key: treeVariant › is deterministic for a given seed

tests.description: The constraint claim of the whole feature: a seed can never sample a parameter outside the declared envelope. A sweep is the only honest way to assert it — one seed proves nothing about the range.
tests.key: treeVariant › keeps every sampled parameter inside TREE_ENVELOPE

tests.description: depth and bareLimb index things, so a fractional draw would be meaningless.
tests.key: treeVariant › rounds the integer ranges to whole numbers

tests.description: The server render and the browser regrow both call this; if they disagreed the regrown tree would be framed differently from the one it replaced.
tests.key: treeViewBox › frames a grown tree identically on repeat calls

tests.description: The frame has to enclose the figure with room for the outermost stroke.
tests.key: treeViewBox › frames the segments with a one unit margin

tests.description: Even at fraction zero at least one move is walked, so nothing renders empty.
tests.key: turtle › always walks at least one move

tests.description: Bookkeeping symbols carry no geometry and must not move the turtle.
tests.key: turtle › ignores symbols that are not moves or turns

tests.description: Forward moves advance along the heading; +x at heading zero.
tests.key: turtle › walks forward along its heading

tests.description: fraction stops the walk partway — this is what makes a fragment a fragment.
tests.key: turtle › walks only part of the moves when fraction is below 1

tests.description: A small cross — a point noted, with no cell worked out around it.
tests.key: unresolvedMarkPath › draws a cross centred on the site

tests.description: Clipping happens beyond the viewBox, which is what lets cells run off the top and bottom unresolved instead of being tidied into a box.
tests.key: voronoiCells › cuts the partition beyond the visible frame

tests.description: A single site owns everything — the degenerate partition, which must still be the whole rectangle rather than an empty list.
tests.key: voronoiCells › gives a lone site the entire frame

tests.description: THE defining property of a Voronoi partition: every point of a cell is nearer that cell's own site than any other. If this does not hold, whatever was drawn is not a Voronoi diagram, however plausible it looks.
tests.key: voronoiCells › gives every cell the territory nearest its own site

tests.description: A partition partitions: the cells must cover the clipped frame exactly, with no gap and no double-counted overlap.
tests.key: voronoiCells › tiles the whole clipped frame without gaps or overlaps

tests.description: Both incompletenesses are deliberate FEATURES, and a feature that silently failed to apply is invisible in a geometry list — the `bareLimbApplied` lesson. So acceptance is told about them rather than left to infer.
tests.key: voronoiShortfall › penalises a field that lost its open cell

tests.description: The unresolved sites are the strongest carrier of "still being worked out".
tests.key: voronoiShortfall › penalises a field with no unresolved sites

tests.description: A sliver is the long thin shard between two sites that landed too close. It reads as a drawing mistake rather than as a boundary, so it is rejected on the geometry that came out — inputs alone cannot catch it.
tests.key: voronoiShortfall › rejects a field containing a sliver

tests.description: A field with nothing drawable can never win the closest-attempt fallback.
tests.key: voronoiShortfall › reports a field with no drawable cells as infinitely short
